types.name: FAssetRefPolicy
types.doc:
What an asset reference is written as (UE's rule that an object path lies
under a mount point). A native absolute path resolves only on the machine
that wrote it — the VFS falls back to the native file when its mounts miss —
so a reference like "C:/Users/<someone>/.../hud.ui" loads for its author,
ships nowhere and names a user in git. The host that knows the mount points
(the open project) installs a normalizer that turns a path under them into
the mount-relative form; what it cannot place stays as it was and is
reported, once per path, when it is written and when a cook resolves it.

types.name: FFieldRedirects
types.doc:
Renames that data on disk still uses — UE's FCoreRedirects, scoped to what
MDF actually needs.

Without this, renaming a reflected field is silent data loss: the stored key
matches no property, so the loader drops the value and logs at DEBUG (once
per key, forever). Renaming a component type is worse — the whole node is
skipped with a warning. A redirect tells the loader where the value went, so
a rename stops costing the user their data.

Entries come from two places: `Register*` at startup (engine renames, which
belong next to the rename that caused them) and a project's
`Config/Redirects.ini`, so a game can declare its own renames without code —
UE's [CoreRedirects] spelling, which the asset registry's renamed asset
paths share:

[CoreRedirects]
+PropertyRedirects=(OldName="LightComponent.colour",NewName="LightComponent.color")
+ClassRedirects=(OldName="PointLight",NewName="LightComponent")
+StructRedirects=(OldName="FOldStats",NewName="FStats")
+EnumRedirects=(OldName="LightType",ValueChanges=(("Omni","Point"),("Sun","Directional")))
+PackageRedirects=(OldName="Content/Old.tex",NewName="Content/New.tex")

An EnumRedirects line that also renames the enum (OldName != NewName) keys
its ValueChanges under the new name, which is what the loader asks with.

The MDF Redirects.mdf it replaces still reads, and converts on first touch
through ConvertLegacy:

Redirects {
Property { type: "LightComponent" from: "colour" to: "color" }
Type { from: "PointLight" to: "LightComponent" }
EnumValue { enum: "LightType" from: "Omni" to: "Point" }

Both serialization paths read them: reflected components and structs, and
actors (an actor's class is a Class redirect, its MPROPERTY a Property
redirect under the class name, an enum value an Enum redirect under the
enum's reflected name).

types.name: FMdfValidator
types.doc:
Document-level MDF validation. Runs AFTER parse, BEFORE
migration/deserialize, and only REPORTS — a diagnosed file still loads
exactly as before (lenient, defaults where safe). Root shape and
schema_version range come from the caller's FMdfRootSchema; component
property type checks ride the reflected TypeDescriptor tables, so a
wrong-typed value the deserializer would silently skip (or a throwing
As<T> would turn into a lost entity) surfaces as a diagnostic with node
path and, for text files, line:column.

Editor engines call SetDefaultEnabled(true); runtime and cooked loads stay
off unless forced via the `mdf.Validate` cvar (-1 = follow the app
default, 0 = force off, 1 = force on).

members.doc:
MOWO_CATEGORY: inspector section this row files under inside its

members.name: assetType
members.doc:
MOWO_ASSET_TYPE: which AssetType an asset-ref row accepts, as the
type's serialized name ("Curve", "Mesh", ...). The inspector filters
its picker by this. It lives on the PROPERTY because the alternative —
an editor-side table keyed by (component name, field name) — has to be
edited every time a field is added, and drifts silently into showing
every asset in the project when a name changes. nullptr = unfiltered.

members.name: units
members.doc:

"deg", "rad", "s", "kg", ...). The inspector shows it as a suffix and
converts where the stored unit is not the one authors think in —
rotation is radians on the wire and degrees in every UI, which every
rotation row used to hand-code against a component name. It lives on the
PROPERTY because the alternative is an editor-side table keyed by
(component, field) that silently goes stale on a rename. nullptr =
unitless.

members.doc:

with structDesc for a struct value). type == Set: setOps, with the
element type in elementType. Keys and set elements are the fixed-width
and string types (Int, UInt32, UUID, String).

Apply a delta produced by BuildDelta into `instance`. Returns fields
applied. Bounds-checked against the descriptor + buffer length (a
malformed/foreign packet stops at the first inconsistency rather than
overrunning), and a delta naming a non-replicable slot is refused
outright — a hostile peer must not be able to talk the receiver into
memcpy'ing over a std::string.

members.doc:
A synthetic row describing one element of an array property, so the
value codec handles elements and fields through the same path. The
element inherits the array's quantizer.

members.signature: static bool IsPackedValueReplicable(const PropertyInfo& p, uint32_t depth)
members.doc:
What the packed codec can carry by value. A struct member that has no
codec refuses the whole struct rather than being skipped: a field that
silently never arrives is the failure this layer exists to prevent.

members.name: WriteScaledFloats
members.signature: static void WriteScaledFloats(FNetBitWriter& w, const float* v, uint32_t count, float scale)
members.doc:
Fixed-point components share one bit width: [1 raw-fallback bit][6-bit
width][count x width bits of zigzag]. A component that is not finite or
does not fit 31 bits after scaling sends the whole vector as raw floats
instead of wrapping into a wrong position.

members.doc:
Smallest three: the largest-magnitude component is dropped (2-bit
index) and rebuilt from the unit norm; the other three lie within
+-1/sqrt(2) and take 15 bits each. 47 bits instead of 128.

Decodes INTO `field`. Only called once the whole delta has been walked
and found in bounds, so a value never lands half-written.

members.signature: static void SkipPackedValue(FNetBitReader& r, const PropertyInfo& p, uint32_t depth)
members.doc:
Walks one value without storing it — the bounds pass. Lengths and counts
are checked against the bits that remain, so a hostile count can never
become an allocation.

members.signature: static void EncodeValue(const PropertyInfo& p, const uint8_t* field, std::vector<uint8_t>& out, uint64_t& outBits)
members.doc:
Exactly what `p`'s current value encodes to — the unit of change
detection. Comparing encodings rather than raw bytes is what lets a
quantized field ignore jitter below its quantum.

members.name: kAudienceNone
members.doc:
Who a delta is being built for, against MNET_CONDITION. kAudienceAll
ignores conditions (tools, tests, the legacy byte form); a sender
building for one peer passes Owner when that peer owns the object and
Initial when the peer has never been sent this component. A field the
audience may not see is left out of the changemask, never zeroed: the
receiver keeps whatever it had, which for an owner-only field on a
non-owner is the default it spawned with.

members.signature: static bool PassesCondition(const PropertyInfo& p, uint32_t audience)

members.name: HasConditionalFields
members.doc:
True when any wire field of `desc` carries a condition, so a sender can
skip building per-audience deltas for the common unconditioned type.

members.name: WritePackedDelta
members.signature: static void WritePackedDelta(const TypeDescriptor* desc, const void* instance, const std::vector<uint8_t>& send, std::vector<uint8_t>& out)
members.doc:
Writes [marker][changemask][values] for the wire fields flagged in
`send` (one entry per wire field, in property order).

members.name: BuildDeltaAgainstEncoded
members.signature: static uint32_t BuildDeltaAgainstEncoded(const TypeDescriptor* desc, const std::vector<uint8_t>& encoded, const void* cur, std::vector<uint8_t>& out, int wantContinuous, uint32_t audience = kAudienceAll)
members.doc:
Packed delta of `cur` against an encoded baseline. `wantContinuous`:
-1 = every replicated field, 0 = discrete only, 1 = continuous only
(strings, arrays and structs count as discrete). A truncated/corrupt
baseline treats the remaining fields as changed — resending is always
safe. Nothing is appended when nothing changed.

members.name: BuildFullFieldSet
members.signature: static uint32_t BuildFullFieldSet(const TypeDescriptor* desc, const void* instance, std::vector<uint8_t>& out, int wantContinuous, uint32_t audience = kAudienceAll)
members.doc:
Every replicated field of `instance` (of the wanted continuity) as one
packed delta — the first-send form, when no baseline exists.

members.name: DecodePackedFieldIndices
members.signature: static bool DecodePackedFieldIndices(const TypeDescriptor* desc, const uint8_t* data, size_t len, std::vector<uint16_t>& outIndices)
members.doc:
The property indices a packed delta carries, read off its changemask —
for tools and tests that need to say WHICH fields crossed the wire.

members.name: ApplyPackedDelta
members.signature: static uint32_t ApplyPackedDelta(const TypeDescriptor* desc, void* instance, const uint8_t* data, size_t len)
members.doc:
Two passes: the first walks every flagged field against the packet's
length and refuses the whole delta on any overrun, the second applies.
Each field's incoming bits are compared with what the receiver's current
value encodes to, so a redundant resend writes nothing and RepNotify
fires only on a real change.

members.signature: static void Serialize(const TypeDescriptor& desc, const void* comp, MdfNode& node)
members.doc:
The node must already carry the correct type name. Calls
desc.customSerialize afterwards when non-null.

members.name: SerializeWithBaseline
members.signature: static void SerializeWithBaseline(const TypeDescriptor& desc, const void* comp, MdfNode& node, const void* baseline)
members.doc:
Delta against an explicit baseline component instead of the CDO —
the prefab-override capture passes the source-built component so the
recorded blob is a true source-delta (per-property override
semantics; propagation resumes for fields reverted to source).

members.name: Deserialize
members.signature: static void Deserialize(const TypeDescriptor& desc, const MdfNode& node, void* comp)
members.doc:
Missing properties are left UNTOUCHED (merge semantics) — correct for
freshly default-constructed components and for prefab-override merges.
Calls desc.customDeserialize afterwards when non-null.

members.name: DeserializeExact
members.signature: static void DeserializeExact(const TypeDescriptor& desc, const MdfNode& node, void* comp)
members.doc:
Exact-restore variant: first resets every serializable POD/String
property to its CDO default (Array/Custom/Struct are skipped — the
serializer always writes those in full), then applies the node. Use when
the node is a STATE SNAPSHOT of a live component (undo/redo): with CDO
delta-serialization a snapshot omits default-valued properties, and a
plain merge-Deserialize would leave current non-default values behind.
RuntimeOnly fields are never touched.

members.name: ForgetCachedTypesInModule
members.doc:
Deserialize logs at DEBUG every key in the node that no reflected
property claims, so a renamed or removed field is visible instead of
silently dropped. The thread-local counter lets tooling assert on that
without scraping the log; it accrues across calls until reset.
The per-type default instance and key set Serialize builds once per
descriptor. Dropped with a descriptor's module (ReflectionRegistry's
unload path calls the first), or all at once.

members.name: FindPropertyBySpelling
members.signature: static const PropertyInfo* FindPropertyBySpelling(const TypeDescriptor& desc, const std::string& key)
members.doc:
The property a hand-written key means when it spells the field the
other way: `cast_shadows` for `castShadows`, or `castShadows` for a
field keyed `cast_shadows`. Case and underscores are ignored; null when
no property matches. Components key some fields snake_case and leave
others under their C++ name, and an author cannot tell which from the
inspector — a correct value under the other spelling was rejected as
an unknown property.

members.name: KeySpellingMatches
members.signature: static bool KeySpellingMatches(const char* fieldName, const std::string& key)
members.doc:
The comparison behind it, for readers keyed by something other than a
TypeDescriptor (actor MPROPERTYs).

members.name: ResetNewerVersionCount
members.doc:
Counts nodes whose `_version` is above what this build's descriptor
knows. Unlike an unknown key — which an old file also produces for a
removed field — this can only mean a newer build wrote the node, so a
document loader reads it to refuse saving over what it could not read.
Thread-local and cumulative until reset, like the unknown-key count.

members.name: NoteNewerVersion
members.doc:
For a serializer with versions of its own (the actor node): counts one
node read from a newer build into the same tally, so the document's
save gate refuses it the same way.

members.name: ExtractUnknownKeys
members.signature: static bool ExtractUnknownKeys(const TypeDescriptor& desc, const MdfNode& node, MdfNode& out)
members.doc:
The keys and child nodes of `node` that no reflected property of `desc`
claims, copied into `out`, so a document owner can hand them back to the
writer: a field a newer build added without bumping the version is
otherwise stripped by the first save from an older build. False, with
`out` untouched, when there is nothing to carry, when the node is older
than the descriptor (its migration owns that shape, and an unclaimed key
there is a removed field), or when the type reads keys the property
table does not name (a custom deserializer or a Custom property).

members.name: MergeUnknownKeys
members.signature: static void MergeUnknownKeys(const MdfNode& carried, MdfNode& node)
members.doc:
Puts back every property and child of `carried` that `node` does not
already hold. What this build wrote always wins.

persist only properties that differ from the defaults.
